# `m.stocks.short_volume`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Daily short sale volume of US-listed stocks, one row per ticker and trading day.

```python
m.stocks.short_volume(symbols=None, *, start=None, end=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

| Verbs | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| Time range | `start` and `end` are sent as `date.gte` and `date.lte` |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `Symbol` and `Date` |
| `sort` | any REST field of the rows (see Massive fields below), or several separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc` |
| `filters` | `short_volume_ratio`, `short_volume_ratio_any_of`, `short_volume_ratio_gt`, `short_volume_ratio_gte`, `short_volume_ratio_lt`, `short_volume_ratio_lte`, `ticker_gt`, `ticker_gte`, `ticker_lt`, `ticker_lte` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `symbols` | Stock tickers; None, the default, for every ticker. | Massive's ticker for each symbol, spelled exactly as Massive spells it: `AAPL` or `BRK.B` for a stock, `O:SPY271217C00700000` (the OCC code) for an option, `I:SPX` for an index, `C:EURUSD` for a forex pair, `X:BTCUSD` for a crypto pair, and `ESZ6` for a future. Pass one symbol as text, several as a list, or a table with a `Symbol` column. A live table is followed: each symbol you add is read, and each one you delete stops being read. `last_by()`, `fetch()`, `history()`, and most polls also drop a deleted symbol's rows. `dm.ALL` reads every symbol, and leaving the argument out reads every record with no filter by symbol, where this dataset takes them. A misspelled symbol in text or a list raises `ValueError` at the call; by default, a misspelled row of a table is skipped and logged, and the table keeps running. `dm.canonical_symbol` converts other spellings to Massive's. A record that lists several symbols, such as a news article, appears once for each symbol you named that it lists. |
| `start` | The first trading day. | The first day or moment of the range. A date (text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`) means the day in the market's time zone: New York for stocks, options, and indices; UTC for forex and crypto; for futures, the trading session that ends that day. An instant is an exact time: a Python `datetime` with a time zone, a `pandas.Timestamp`, a `numpy.datetime64`, a Deephaven `Instant` or `ZonedDateTime`, or Deephaven time text such as `"2025-06-02T09:30 ET"`. Give `start` and `end` as two dates or two instants. A `datetime` without a time zone raises `ValueError`, and a calendar-date field, such as an ex-dividend date, takes dates only. |
| `end` | The last trading day. | The last day, or the moment the range stops, in the same form as `start`. A date includes its whole day, so `start="2025-06-02", end="2025-06-02"` reads all of June 2; an instant is excluded. Leave it out to read through now; a list dataset then sends Massive no end, so it also returns records still to come, such as dividends announced but not yet paid. |
| `sort` | The field to sort by, such as `"date"`. | The field to order the rows by, named as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Where the endpoint allows, name several, separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc`: `"ticker,ex_dividend_date.desc"`. This page lists the values the dataset takes. |
| `order` | The direction of `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows to return, in total. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | Further endpoint parameters, such as `{"short_volume_ratio_gte": 50}`. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `ticker`: "The primary ticker symbol for the stock." | REST |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. | REST |
| `AdfShortVolume` | long | Short volume reported via the Alternative Display Facility (ADF), excluding exempt volume. | REST |
| `AdfShortVolumeExempt` | long | Short volume reported via ADF that was marked as exempt. | REST |
| `Date` | String | The date of trade activity reported in the format YYYY-MM-DD | REST |
| `ExemptVolume` | double | Portion of short volume that was marked as exempt from regulation SHO. | REST |
| `NasdaqCarteretShortVolume` | long | Short volume reported from Nasdaq's Carteret facility, excluding exempt volume. | REST |
| `NasdaqCarteretShortVolumeExempt` | long | Short volume from Nasdaq Carteret that was marked as exempt. | REST |
| `NasdaqChicagoShortVolume` | long | Short volume reported from Nasdaq's Chicago facility, excluding exempt volume. | REST |
| `NasdaqChicagoShortVolumeExempt` | long | Short volume from Nasdaq Chicago that was marked as exempt. | REST |
| `NonExemptVolume` | double | Portion of short volume that was not exempt from regulation SHO (i.e., short_volume - exempt_volume). | REST |
| `NyseShortVolume` | long | Short volume reported from NYSE facilities, excluding exempt volume. | REST |
| `NyseShortVolumeExempt` | long | Short volume from NYSE facilities that was marked as exempt. | REST |
| `ShortVolume` | double | Total number of shares sold short across all venues for the ticker on the given date. | REST |
| `ShortVolumeRatio` | double | The percentage of total volume that was sold short. Calculated as (short_volume / total_volume) * 100. | REST |
| `TotalVolume` | double | Total reported volume across all venues for the ticker on the given date. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
